answer: Only a coat cut to the tailor's own measure book earns a seat. The book holds the chest, the shoulder and the sleeve of every man in the parish, measured anew each spring. A pigment coat bought ready-made fails the book: at the vertex of the shoulder the cloth must follow the customer's own numbers, and a strange coat pulls or sags. Faking a measure means bribing a tailor, measuring a hundred men and paying 6,700, while the quill entry in the book is checked at every fitting, so a coat cut to no measure is given away.
